title: World-Shaper: A Unified Framework for 360° Panoramic Editing
claim: One unified model handles generation and many editing operations, producing coherent, high-quality results across diverse scenes and instructions.
layout: Gallery mosaic: wide editing panel left, generation panels right, instruction captions below
description: A gallery-style figure on a white background. The top-left blue banner reads 'Panoramic Image Editing' and sits above a large before/after pair of a cartoon wheat-field panorama. On the left, white boxes mark where objects will go. On the right, a scarecrow, a deer and a cat appear, with zoomed insets. The user instruction is quoted below with 'Add' in red. Beneath that, a 2x3 grid of indoor and outdoor panoramas shows originals on top and edited versions below. Edits include replace, change and move, each with red-boxed zoom insets and a quoted instruction. The right column has a yellow 'Text-to-Panorama Generation' banner over an apartment interior. A green 'Image-to-Panorama Generation' banner sits over a small input patch on black, then the generated Gothic mansion panorama. Small user icons precede each prompt.
caption: Our geometry-aware diffusion framework, World-Shaper, unifies panorama generation and editing within a single editing-centric model, supporting text-to-panorama and image-to-panorama generation, and diverse editing operations such as object addition, removal, replacement, relocation, and appearance modification. New objects and edited regions are highlighted in white and red boxes, respectively.
abstract: Being able to edit panoramic images is crucial for creating realistic 360Â° visual experiences. However, existing perspective-based image editing methods fail to model the spatial structure of panoramas. Conventional cube-map decompositions attempt to overcome this problem but inevitably break global consistency due to their mismatch with spherical geometry. Motivated by this insight, we reformulate panoramic editing directly in the equirectangular projection (ERP) domain and present World-Shaper, a unified geometry-aware framework that bridges panoramic generation and editing within a single editing-centric design. To overcome the scarcity of paired data, we adopt a generate-then-edit paradigm, where controllable panoramic generation serves as an auxiliary stage to synthesize diverse paired examples for supervised editing learning. To address geometric distortion, we introduce a geometry-aware learning strategy that explicitly enforces position-aware shape supervision and implicitly internalizes panoramic priors through progressive training. Extensive experiments on our new benchmark, PEBench, demonstrate that our method achieves superior geometric consistency, editing fidelity, and text controllability compared to SOTA methods, enabling coherent and flexible 360Â° visual world creation with unified editing control. Code, model, and data will be released at our project page: https://world-shaper-project.github.io/
